tagline: Fifteen miles through a narrowing canyon to Utah ski country
intro: Big Cottonwood Canyon Scenic Byway heads east on SR-190 from the canyon mouth, with the walls closing in almost immediately. Visit Utah lists this state scenic byway as a 15-mile, 25-minute drive and highlights its alpine scenery, old mining country and recreation. Trailheads, picnic areas, cabins and historic water and mining works line the canyon route. Big Cottonwood Creek formed the V-shaped canyon, with its many rock formations.

The highway developed in stages: part of the present route entered the state system in 1933 as SR-152, reaching the national forest boundary. That designation extended to Brighton in 1941. In 1963, an extension followed an existing county road over Guardsman Pass to provide access to the new Wasatch Mountain State Park. The canyon section became SR-190 in 1987.

From the canyon mouth, the drive passes Stairs Station, a hydroelectric plant built in 1894–1895, before reaching Solitude and the loop through Brighton. The Forest Service identifies Silver Lake and its visitor center among the destinations reached by the drive. For a summer continuation toward Park City, the connection to Guardsman Pass requires some backtracking from the Brighton loop and follows a narrower mountain road. That crossing normally closes all winter.

moments.title: Stairs Station
moments.text: Stairs Station was built in 1894–1895 to generate hydroelectric power. Robert M. Jones designed the station for his Big Cottonwood Power Company, which contracted in 1895 to supply the Salt Lake and Ogden Gas and Electric Company. Its two-story powerhouse placed generating equipment below and switchgear above. Four original Pelton wheels have given way to one Francis turbine. The powerhouse is the plant’s only remaining building, part of a system that also includes penstocks and a pipeline. Its Second Renaissance Revival design gives this industrial site an architectural identity of its own.

moments.title: Doughnut Falls
moments.text: Doughnut Falls drops into a pothole in the rock, with an arch above the pool. The waterfall lies near Silver Fork in Big Cottonwood Canyon, reached from the Mill D Trailhead toward the Jordan Pines picnic area. The summer hike is about 1.5 miles round trip if parking is available; a different winter approach can take up to 3.5 miles round trip.

moments.title: Brighton
moments.text: An old elevator motor helped launch Brighton’s ski area. In 1936, Alpine Ski Club members combined it with wire to build a rope tow, beginning what became Utah’s first ski resort. The town occupies the top of Big Cottonwood Canyon and includes both Brighton and Solitude ski resorts. The area was first settled in 1871. Its municipal story is much newer than its skiing: residents voted to incorporate in November 2018, and incorporation took effect on January 1, 2020. SR-190 makes a loop through Brighton before connecting, with backtracking, to the Guardsman Pass road.

practical: Brighton: The Guardsman Pass continuation normally closes all winter. (checked 2026-10-11)
